items.title: Section: The Four Right Efforts Open, Continuing Directly from the Foundations

items.zh: 如是於四念住串習行故，已能除遣麁麁顛倒，已能了達善不善法。從此無間，於諸未生惡不善法，為不生故；於諸已生惡不善法，為令斷故；於其未生一切善法，為令生故；於其已生一切善法，為欲令住、令不忘失，廣說如前；乃至攝心、持心。
items.en: Within the Basic Section, in the Ground of the Hearer-Disciples, the fourth part of the second yogic process … Thus, through repeated practice of the four foundations of mindfulness, one becomes able to dispel the coarsest of the distorted views, and becomes able to clearly distinguish wholesome states from unwholesome ones. Immediately following this, one strives — in order to prevent unwholesome states not yet arisen from arising; to end unwholesome states already arisen; to give rise to wholesome states not yet arisen; and to make wholesome states already arisen abide and not be forgotten — as has been extensively explained before, spurring and sustaining the mind.

items.title: What Counts as Unwholesome; Arisen and Unarisen

items.zh: 云何名為惡不善法？謂欲纏染污身語意業，是身語意惡行所攝，及能起彼所有煩惱。若未和合、未現在前，說名未生；若已和合、已現在前，說名已生。
items.en: What is called an evil, unwholesome state? It is bodily, verbal, and mental action defiled by the manifest afflictions bound to the desire realm — action classed as bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct — together with all the afflictions capable of giving rise to such misconduct. Whatever has not yet come together through conditions, not yet appearing before one, is called unarisen; whatever has already come together through conditions, already appearing before one, is called arisen.

items.title: What Counts as Wholesome; Generating the Aspiration

items.zh: 云何名為一切善法？謂若彼對治、若蓋對治、若結對治。未生、已生，應知如前惡不善法。若時未生惡不善法，先未和合，為令不生，發起希願：我當令彼一切一切皆不復生。是名於諸未生惡不善法，為不生故生欲。若時已生惡不善法，先已和合，為令斷故，發起希願：我當於彼一切一切皆不忍受，斷滅、除遣。是名於諸已生惡不善法，為令斷故生欲。
items.en: What is called every kind of wholesome state? It is whatever counters ordinary affliction, whatever counters the hindrances, and whatever counters the fetters. Arisen and unarisen should be understood as with the unwholesome states above. When an unwholesome state has not yet arisen, its conditions not yet come together, one generates the aspiration, for the sake of its not arising: "May I ensure this, and everything like it, never arises at all." This is generating the aspiration, for unarisen unwholesome states, that they not arise. When an unwholesome state has already arisen, its conditions already come together, one generates the aspiration, for the sake of ending it: "I will not tolerate this, or anything like it, at all — I will cut it off, remove it, and expel it." This is generating the aspiration, for arisen unwholesome states, that they be ended.

items.zh: 又彼一切惡不善法，或緣過去事生、或緣未來事生、或緣現在事生。如是彼法，或緣不現見境、或緣現見境。若緣過去、未來事境，是名緣不現見境；若緣現在事境，是名緣現見境。

items.title: Self-Spurring and Diligent Effort: Three Ways of Drawing the Line

items.zh: 當知此中，於緣不現見境惡不善法，其未生者欲令不生，其已生者欲令永斷，自策、自勵，是名策勵。於緣現見境惡不善法，其未生者欲令不生，其已生者欲令永斷，勇猛正勤，是名發勤精進。所以者何？要當堅固，自策、自勵，勇猛正勤，方能令彼或不復生、或永斷滅。又於下品、中品諸纏，其未生者欲令不生，其已生者欲令永斷，故自策勵。於上品纏，其未生者欲令不生，其已生者欲令永斷，發勤精進。又若行於過去境界，如是行時，不令煩惱緣彼生起；設復失念暫時生起，而不忍受，速能斷滅、除遣、變吐。如緣過去，若行未來，當知亦爾。如是未生惡不善法能令不生，生已能斷，是名策勵。若行現在所緣境界，如是行時、不令煩惱緣彼生起；設復失念暫時生起，而不忍受，速能斷滅、除遣、變吐。如是未生惡不善法能令不生，生已能斷，是名發勤精進。
items.en: Know that here: regarding unwholesome states connected to an object not directly seen … spurring and rousing oneself is called self-spurring. Regarding unwholesome states connected to an object directly seen … courageous and correct exertion is called diligent effort. Further, regarding entanglements of the lower and middling grades … one spurs oneself. Regarding entanglements of the upper grade … one exerts diligent effort. Further, when engaging with a past object … this is called self-spurring. When engaging with a presently experienced object … this is called diligent effort.

items.title: Section: A Fourth Framework Closes the First Two Right Efforts

items.zh: 又或有惡不善法，唯由分別力生，非境界力；或有惡不善法，由分別力生，亦境界力。唯由分別力生，非境界力者，謂於住時，思惟過去、未來境界而生於彼。由思惟力生，亦境界力者，謂於行時，緣現在境界而生於彼。當於爾時，決定亦有非理分別。當知此中，惡不善法唯由分別力生，非境界力者，彼若未生能令不生，生已能斷，是名策勵。若由分別力生，亦境界力者，彼若未生能令不生，生已能斷，是名發勤精進。
items.en: Further, some unwholesome states arise solely through the power of discrimination, not through the power of an object; some unwholesome states arise through the power of discrimination together with the power of an object. Know that here: where an unwholesome state arises solely through the power of discrimination, not the power of an object … this is called self-spurring. Where it arises through the power of discrimination together with the power of an object … this is called diligent effort.

blocks.text: Fascicle 29 completes the thirty-seven factors of awakening (right efforts, bases of power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, eightfold path), then answers the last questions: the fruit of cultivation, kinds of practitioner, synonyms, Māra, and why effort may bear no fruit.

subs.head: From the foundations to the efforts

blocks.text: "Through repeated practice of the four foundations of mindfulness, one becomes able to dispel the coarsest of distortions", and so moves on to the right efforts.
"Bodily, verbal, and mental action defiled by the manifest afflictions bound to the desire realm." Master Cháng Bǎi: expressed, it is misconduct; unexpressed, it is still unwholesome.

"Whatever counters ordinary affliction, the hindrances, and the fetters." Venerable Miào Jìng: a fetter "joins you with suffering". For an unwholesome state not yet arisen, "its conditions not yet come together, one generates the aspiration" that it not arise; for one that has arisen, that it be abandoned.

"Spurring and rousing oneself is called self-spurring." The treatise draws the line in several ways: for objects not directly present, self-spurring; for objects present, diligent effort; and by grade, from subtle to coarse.

"Some unwholesome states arise solely through the power of discrimination, not through an object"; some through both. Master Cháng Bǎi: the sense consciousnesses only cognise; the key is the discriminating mind.

quiz.q: Why do the right efforts follow the foundations of mindfulness, and where does Master Cháng Bǎi say the drive for effort comes from?
options: after repeated mindfulness practice one dispels coarse distortions and discerns good from bad; having tasted the Dharma, a joy beyond sense pleasure
quiz.why: "Thus, through repeated practice of the four foundations of mindfulness, one becomes able to dispel the coarsest of the distorted views, and becomes able to clearly distinguish wholesome states from unwholesome ones." Master Cháng Bǎi: one can be diligent because one has tasted the flavour of the Dharma; the more one practices, the richer it gets — a joy surpassing the five sense pleasures.

quiz.q: What is an evil, unwholesome state, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish "evil" from "unwholesome"?
options: defiled action of body, speech, mind and the afflictions behind it; "evil" drags to bad realms, "unwholesome" does great harm
quiz.why: "What is called an evil, unwholesome state? It is bodily, verbal, and mental action defiled by the manifest afflictions bound to the desire realm." Venerable Miào Jìng: it makes one fall into bad realms, hence "evil"; it does great harm to you, hence "unwholesome."

quiz.q: What three counters make up "every wholesome state," and how does Venerable Miào Jìng map them?
options: countering affliction, the hindrances, the fetters; the latter two are calm and insight, the first is discipline
quiz.why: "What is called every kind of wholesome state? It is whatever counters ordinary affliction, whatever counters the hindrances, and whatever counters the fetters." Venerable Miào Jìng: countering the hindrances and the fetters are calm and insight; countering "those" is discipline.

quiz.q: One "generates the aspiration" that unarisen evil not arise. What does Venerable Miào Jìng draw from this?
options: not just Pure Land — every Dharma path has faith, vow, and practice
quiz.why: "When an unwholesome state has not yet arisen, its conditions not yet come together, one generates the aspiration, for the sake of its not arising." Venerable Miào Jìng: it is not only the Pure Land path — every path has faith, vow, and practice.

quiz.q: In the first way of distinguishing self-spurring from diligent effort, what does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: both are effort; self-spurring concerns unseen objects, diligent effort seen ones
quiz.why: "Spurring and rousing oneself is called self-spurring." Master Cháng Bǎi: both are effort; self-spurring takes objects not directly seen, diligent effort takes objects directly seen.

quiz.q: Some unwholesome states arise "solely through discrimination." Which consciousness does Venerable Miào Jìng assign this to?
options: only the mental consciousness, not the five senses, which contact outer objects
quiz.why: "Some unwholesome states arise solely through the power of discrimination, not through the power of an object." Venerable Miào Jìng: this belongs solely to the mental consciousness, not the five senses — those contact external objects, while the sixth does not take them directly.

quiz.q: For states arising from discrimination "together with an object," how do the masters see the senses and the mind?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the senses only cognize, the main culprit is the sixth's improper discrimination; Miào Jìng: object-driven evil spans all consciousnesses
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the five sense consciousnesses do not discriminate on their own; they only cognize — the key is the sixth consciousness's improper discrimination. Venerable Miào Jìng: unwholesome states arising by the power of objects extend to all consciousnesses, not only the five.
